messages:
incidents-bot: SEV2 alert — gpu-pool-eu-west reports sustained saturation and growing request queue (90m). Autoscaler attempted scale but failed repeatedly. Paging oncall.

maya (oncall): I’m on it. Starting a short bridge, pinging infra. Can anyone grab the live grafana link?

alex: grabbing now — https://grafana.redwood.svc/d/gpu-pools/gpu-pool-eu-west?orgId=1 : queue length spiked ~03:22 UTC, currently ~12k waiting requests, token rate trending up. latency p50->p95 divergence.

ravi: logs show autoscaler POST to cloud-provider returned 403 quota-exceeded at 03:24:11. repeated attempts. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:24:11Z scaler.go:214 -> cloudapi.CreateInstance: 403 QuotaExceeded: cpus-per-project quota reached
request id: x-req-9b2
```

kim: we have a pending quota request but not approved. autoscaler doesn't have a fallback pool configured for this pool (it expects scaleHoriz to work). That explains why requests piled up instead of routing to warm standby.

maya (oncall): Ok. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle non-urgent requests (set ingress rate limit to 50%), 2) route critical customers to a fallback smaller-quantized model in a different pool, 3) start manual provisioning if possible. Alex — can you toggle throttling? Ravi — can you confirm which customers are critical?

alex: toggled global route throttle to 50% for gpu-pool-eu-west :thumbsup:

chloe: FYI CS reports two enterprise customers saw degraded responses (ingest/embedding jobs delayed). Waiting for exact customer list from CS.

ravi: critical customers: acme-inc, beta-ml, zenhealth. We can selectively route acme-inc and beta-ml to eu-west-small-quant pool which has capacity for limited burst.

maya (oncall): Routing acme-inc + beta-ml now via policy -> eu-west-small-quant. Confirmed start to see dequeue on those customer queues.

ops-bot: Manual provision attempt blocked — cloud provider API returning quota error, same 403. ETA from provider on quota not known.

alex: autoscaler process shows heartbeat misses to control plane around 03:20-03:26. Oncall logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:21:03Z agent-heartbeat: timeout
2026-03-15T03:21:03Z autoscaler: attempt scale -> cloudapi failed
```
Could be control-plane network blip + quota combo.

maya (oncall): Good catch. Prioritizing two tracks in parallel: 1) mitigate customer-facing impact (throttle + routing) 2) restore autoscaler/scale path (investigate heartbeat / cloud quota). Alex drop the scaledown settings so nothing gets torn down.

alex: set scaleDownDisabled=true for gpu-pool-eu-west to avoid oscillation.

ravi: forensic note — autoscaler tried to create 6 nodes, cloud returned quota exceeded after 2. We now have partial capacity but not enough.

chloe: CS confirmed acme-inc reported reduced success rate for bulk-embed job; they have 1200 queued tasks. Beta-ml had 300 queued. Zenhealth queued but lower priority and currently throttled.

maya (oncall): Estimate customer impact window: start 03:22 UTC, alleviated partial 03:30 for routed customers, system-level backlog continues. Potential customer-visible disruption ~8-40 minutes depending on queue position.

alex: starting short bridgecall now — dial-in 10.0.0.5:4000, I’ll put notes in the calendar.

ravi: attaching relevant autoscaler logs for postmortem copy-paste:
```
--- autoscaler.log ---
03:20:59 scaler: reconcile start
03:21:05 scaler: attempt scale +6 -> cloudapi.CreateInstance -> 403 QuotaExceeded
03:22:10 scaler: heartbeat lost -> controller comms timeout
03:24:35 scaler: backoff reset
```

maya (oncall): Quick customer comms: @chloe please push a short note to affected customers: "We're experiencing higher than normal GPU queueing in eu-west; limited impact to a subset of customers — we've routed mission-critical traffic and applied temporary throttles. We will follow up with incident summary." Keep it brief.

chloe: sending now. draft: "We're seeing temporary queuing on GPU workloads in eu-west. We've enacted throttling and rerouted priority jobs; some jobs may be delayed. We're investigating and will follow up with a post-incident summary." sending to acme-inc, beta-ml, zenhealth.

ops-bot: FYI automated runbook suggestions: consider adding warm standby pool + pre-warm on spike detection; add quota checks to autoscaler preflight.

maya (oncall): Agreed. For immediate further mitigation: 1) open emergency quota request with provider (alex) 2) create warm-standby policy ticket (ravi) 3) post-incident followup + alert tuning (maya). Who can own quota request?

alex: I'll open emergency ticket and escalate with our vendor contact. ETA unknown but raised now.

ravi: I'll file warm-standby design ticket with ops and scheduling; will include cost/ops tradeoffs.

maya (oncall):Thanks. Monitoring queue — seeing slow taper down. Current queue now ~3.2k. Continue watching for 30m. Once stable, we'll close the incident and track follow-ups.

chloe: customers acknowledged comms. acme-inc asked for timeline; I told them we'll update in 60 minutes with details.

maya (oncall): Closing notes before handoff: severity -> SEV2. Root symptoms: autoscaler attempted scale but cloud quota prevented node creation AND brief control-plane heartbeat issues prevented fallback routing. Primary impact: request queueing and delays for non-prioritized customers; limited impact to routed critical customers.

maya (oncall): Handoff to Alex (primary) and Ravi (infra follow-up). Action items in thread:
- alex: escalate quota with cloud provider, capture ticket id. (owner)
- ravi: implement autoscaler preflight quota check + warm-standby design. (owner)
- maya: write incident timeline and coordinate postmortem with CS notes. (owner)
- chloe: customer comms and follow-up.

alex: ack. ticket #CLOUD-7890 opened and escalated to support engineer. keeping it open until quotas increase.

ravi: ack. filing ticket now: INFRA-1457 (warm-standby & preflight). Estimated 2 sprints for design + 1 for rollout with automation.

chloe: ack. will send follow-up update to customers after postmortem draft.

maya (oncall): handing off. last check-in in 30m or on new alerts. Good job team. :heart:

incidents-bot: Incident marked resolved for oncall – manual handoff completed. Please file postmortem within 72h.

maya (oncall): Postmortem TODOs (short): timeline + decision points, root cause hypothesis (quota + heartbeat), mitigation implemented (throttle + routing + scaleDownDisabled toggle), action items assigned, follow-up owners. I’ll create the doc.

alex: adding logs and grafana snapshots to the postmortem doc.

ravi: will include suggested autoscaler code snippet for preflight (pseudo):
```
func canScale(reqNodes int) bool {
  quotas := cloud.GetQuota(project)
  return quotas.availableCpus >= reqNodes*nodeCpu
}
```

maya (oncall): Great. Closing thread.
